quizzes.title: MC14 Disputes, Farm and Fisheries Talks
quizzes.passage:
The 14th Ministerial Conference of the World Trade Organization was held in Yaoundé, Cameroon, and it ended without consensus. The disagreement reflected a deep North-South divide among members. Several agendas were left unresolved, and the matters that could not be settled were passed on to a later meeting.

The WTO's mandate covers trade in goods, services and intellectual property. Its Ministerial Conference is the highest decision-making body and is made up of trade ministers and senior officials from member nations. It addresses global trade developments. WTO decisions are traditionally sought through agreement among all members.

One of the agendas before the conference was the reform of the WTO's dispute settlement system, which helps resolve trade disputes among members. The reform was among the agendas that remained contested.

Agriculture and food security formed another contested agenda. Food security was treated as a central concern, and positions on the topic differed among members. The discussions reflected the concerns of several countries, including developing ones.

Fisheries was a third agenda. The negotiations dealt with subsidies given to fishing, and members discussed the limits that might apply to them. Some questions on fisheries subsidies were not finished when the conference closed, and the talks were set to continue.

questions.q: Which kind of dispute settlement system is the reform meant to restore?
questions.explanation: The booklet says the reform seeks to restore a two-tier binding dispute system.

questions.q: Where were the key issues left unresolved at MC14 deferred to?
questions.explanation: The key issues were deferred to a WTO General Council meeting in Geneva.

questions.q: On expanding flexibilities for public stockholding (PSH), where do developed countries stand?
options: They have already eliminated the flexibilities
They are eager to expand the flexibilities
They remain reluctant to expand the flexibilities
They have referred the matter to a dispute panel
questions.explanation: The booklet states that developed countries remain reluctant to expand PSH flexibilities.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): The fisheries talks target a ban on harmful subsidies.
Reason (R): The fisheries talks have already completed such a ban at MC14.
options: A is true, but R is false
Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is false, but R is true
questions.explanation: The booklet says members only agreed to continue fisheries negotiations, so the ban has not been completed.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. India and African nations   ->   A. Permanent solution for public stockholding
II. Developing countries   ->   B. Climate-related disruptions
III. Agriculture talks   ->   C. Reducing trade-distorting subsidies
IV. Distant-water fishing fleets   ->   D. Continued negotiations on curbing subsidies
questions.explanation: Each pair matches a demand, challenge or agenda item stated in the booklet.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. Market access is described as crucial for developing countries like India.
II. Developed countries have already agreed to expand PSH flexibilities.
III. The key issues include flexibility for domestic food subsidies and protection against penalties under WTO rules.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement II is incorrect because developed countries remain reluctant to expand PSH flexibilities.

questions.q:
How many of the following statements are correct?
I. The agriculture talks seek to improve market access.
II. The fisheries talks have already completed a ban on harmful subsidies.
III. The dispute settlement reform aims to restore a single-tier advisory system.
questions.explanation: Only statement I matches the booklet, since the fisheries ban is still a target and the reform aims for a two-tier system.

quizzes.title: MC14 Disputes, Farm and Fisheries Talks
quizzes.passage:
The 14th Ministerial Conference of the WTO was held in Yaoundé, Cameroon, and it ended without consensus. The disagreement reflected a deep North-South divide among members. Several agendas were left open when the meeting closed, and the matters that could not be settled were carried forward to a later meeting.

The dispute settlement system is central to the WTO because it helps members resolve trade disputes. Reform of the system was one of the main agendas before the conference, and the reform aims to restore a binding dispute system.

Agriculture and food security was another contested agenda. Food security was treated as a central concern, and positions on the topic differed among members. The agriculture agenda also covered the reduction of certain subsidies and the question of market access.

Fisheries was a third agenda. The negotiations dealt with subsidies given to the fishing sector, and members discussed how such support might be limited. Some of these subsidy questions remained open when the conference closed, and members agreed to keep negotiating them.

The Ministerial Conference, the organisation's highest decision-making body, is made up of trade ministers and senior officials from member nations and addresses global trade developments. The WTO's mandate covers trade in goods, services and intellectual property.

questions.q: How many tiers does the dispute settlement system that the reform aims to restore have? (one word)
questions.explanation: The booklet calls it a two-tier binding dispute system.

questions.q: To which WTO body were the issues left unresolved at MC14 deferred? (two words)
questions.explanation: Key issues were deferred to a WTO General Council meeting in Geneva.

questions.q: In agriculture talks, what does the acronym PSH stand for? (first two words)
questions.explanation: PSH stands for public stockholding for food security.

questions.q: Along with India, which group of nations reiterated the demand for a permanent solution on PSH? (one word)
questions.explanation: India and African nations reiterated the demand for a permanent solution on public stockholding.

questions.q: For which fishing fleets did members agree to keep negotiating subsidy curbs? (one hyphenated word)
questions.explanation: Members agreed to continue negotiations on curbing subsidies for distant-water fishing fleets.

questions.q: Besides overfishing, what problem do harmful fisheries subsidies cause? (one word)
questions.explanation: The booklet says harmful fisheries subsidies cause overcapacity and overfishing.

questions.q: Besides market access barriers, what kind of disruptions do developing countries face? (one word)
questions.explanation: The booklet lists climate-related disruptions as a challenge for developing countries.

quizzes.title: Investment Facilitation Agreement Debate
quizzes.passage:
The Investment Facilitation for Development Agreement is one of the WTO's most debated pacts, and its place within the organisation has been contested. Supporters see it as part of a wider shift in the WTO toward plurilateralism. The debate also reflects how investment is governed globally, and the arrangement moves toward standardised investment rules.

The agreement is discussed in relation to a balance between investment facilitation and national sovereignty. A concern raised in the debate is that the agreement could dilute core WTO principles and expand the organisation's mandate beyond trade facilitation. Members at different stages of development have a stake in this discussion. The discussion also involves how far investment rules should bind members, and which subjects fall within the WTO's remit. These questions are central to the debate.

The WTO's mandate covers trade in goods, services and intellectual property, and the organisation provides a framework for reducing trade restrictions such as tariffs and quotas. It also oversees mechanisms for resolving trade disputes among members.

The Ministerial Conference is the highest decision-making body of the WTO and is made up of trade ministers and senior officials from member nations. The General Council provides administrative and technical support to WTO bodies, and the Secretariat supports the organisation's work.

questions.q: What is the stated objective of the IFD Agreement?
options: To liberalise market access for goods
To make investment procedures transparent, efficient and predictable
To replace all bilateral investment treaties
questions.explanation: The booklet says the objective is to make investment procedures transparent, efficient and predictable.

questions.q: Which of the following is excluded from the scope of the IFD Agreement?
questions.explanation: The booklet says the agreement excludes government procurement, along with market access, investment protection and investor-state dispute settlement.

questions.q: For which group of countries does the IFD's facilitation of foreign direct investment particularly focus?
questions.explanation: The booklet says the focus is on facilitating FDI, especially for developing and least developed countries.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): India opposed bringing the IFD Agreement into the WTO's multilateral framework.
Reason (R): India holds that investment is not strictly a trade subject and so lies outside the WTO's core mandate.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.explanation: The booklet lists the mandate concern among India's reasons for opposing the agreement's inclusion.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. Firewall clause   ->   A. Prevents IFD rules from overriding BITs
II. Appeal mechanism   ->   B. Requires independent tribunals for dispute review
III. Launch   ->   C. Under a Joint Statement Initiative at MC11
IV. Basis of the agreement   ->   D. Most-Favoured-Nation principle
questions.explanation: Each pair matches the booklet's description of the firewall clause, appeal mechanism, launch and basis of the agreement.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. The IFD Agreement covers investment facilitation, including procedures, approvals and transparency.
II. The IFD Agreement includes market access commitments.
III. The appeal mechanism of the IFD Agreement requires independent tribunals for dispute review.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement II is incorrect because the agreement excludes market access.

questions.q:
How many of the following statements are correct?
I. The IFD Agreement was launched at MC11 in Buenos Aires.
II. The IFD Agreement excludes investor-state dispute settlement.
III. The IFD Agreement is based on the principle of reciprocity.
questions.explanation: The booklet supports statements I and II, while it names the Most-Favoured-Nation principle rather than reciprocity.

quizzes.title: Investment Facilitation Agreement Debate
quizzes.passage:
The Investment Facilitation for Development Agreement is among the WTO's most debated pacts, and its place within the organisation has been contested. Supporters see it as part of a wider movement in the WTO toward arrangements among a subset of members. Some members question whether investment belongs within the organisation's core mandate.

The agreement aims to improve how investment procedures work, and it is linked to the broader question of how investment is governed globally, including the move toward standardised investment rules. Developing countries and least developed countries are part of this discussion.

The debate also touches on sovereignty. Members have to weigh the benefits of investment facilitation against the policy space that governments want to keep for their own regulation. A concern raised in the discussions is that the agreement could dilute core WTO principles and expand the organisation's mandate beyond trade facilitation. Such questions are central to the debate.

The WTO itself was established on January 1, 1995, and it facilitates trade in goods, services and intellectual property. Its Ministerial Conference, made up of trade ministers and senior officials, is the organisation's highest decision-making body. The organisation also has a Secretariat and a General Council. Members also have different views on how the agreement fits within the organisation's structure.

questions.q: Under what kind of initiative was the IFD launched? (acronym)
questions.explanation: The IFD was launched under a Joint Statement Initiative at MC11.

questions.q: In which city was the MC11 Ministerial Conference, where the IFD was launched, held? (city)
questions.explanation: MC11 was held in Buenos Aires in 2017.

questions.q: On which principle is the IFD Agreement based? (acronym)
questions.explanation: The booklet says the IFD Agreement is based on the Most-Favoured-Nation principle.

questions.q: The firewall clause stops IFD rules from overriding which kind of treaties? (acronym)
questions.explanation: The firewall clause prevents IFD rules from overriding Bilateral Investment Treaties.

questions.q: On which principle does the WTO traditionally work, which JSIs were seen as bypassing? (one word)
questions.explanation: The WTO traditionally works on consensus of all members, which JSIs were seen to bypass.

questions.q: Majority supporters of the IFD are linked to which initiative? (acronym)
questions.explanation: The booklet links majority supporters to the Belt and Road Initiative, which raises strategic concerns for India.

questions.q: What kind of tribunals must the IFD's appeal mechanism require for dispute review? (one word)
questions.explanation: The appeal mechanism requires independent tribunals for dispute review.
